acceptanceCriteria: A retained measurement reports CPU seconds per hook event (session-start, user-prompt, stop) on a large dirty worktree and idle CPU per minute of each long-running corvint-tasks process with no work.
Busy polling, repeated full scans and redundant re-hashing/re-probing found on those paths are removed or justified in the spec; idle long-running processes use well under 1% of one CPU.
A maintained benchmark or test guards the fixed hot paths against regression.
body:
Filed 2026-10-06 by the orchestrator session.

Owner, 2026-10-06: we should always be efficient and not eat CPU unless absolutely essential. Observed: load peaked at 164 while queue writers ran full-history audits (#641); dogfood hook events probe the repository twice (V1-0881); the dispatcher samples every tick. No CPU budget is measured or enforced for hooks, long-running processes (dispatch, lane-leader, user service) or idle states.
